quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten the handlebars, then stop.
Apply both brakes hard while still leaning.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the handlebars, then stop.
questions.explanation: First straighten the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten the motorcycle, apply the brakes smoothly and gently. Reduce your lean angle and increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then reapply the brake.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops completely.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops completely.
questions.explanation: Do not release the rear brake if it locks. Keep it locked until the motorcycle comes to a complete stop.

questions.question: How can you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep using the rear brake.
Swerve toward the safest area.
Try to accelerate while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Release the brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, if the rear brake locks on a dry road, you can keep it locked until the motorcycle stops.

questions.question: When another rider passes you from behind, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Move to the shoulder of the road.
Use the left part of your lane.
Use the center part of your lane.
Use the right part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center part of your lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may make the driver return to your lane unsafely.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast the alcohol is consumed
The drinker's body weight
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight. How often someone drinks does not affect BAC. Never drive under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on long rides, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Dress warmly.
Limit how far you ride each day.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: Dress for bad weather to stay comfortable. Ride no more than six hours a day and take a break every two hours. Avoid artificial stimulants because you will feel extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should always be avoided?

options.text: The left part of the lane
The center part of the lane
The right part of the lane
No part of the lane should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part of the lane should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best or always worst. Choose a lane position based on current riding conditions.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders do about hearing protection?

options.text: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Wear hearing protection only on long rides.
Do not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Do not need hearing protection if wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Earplugs protect your hearing while still allowing you to hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your fingers near the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch in when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers near the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your fingers near the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. This is especially helpful when riding through areas with potential hazards.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need in traffic?

options.text: Much less than cars
Less than cars
The same as cars
More than cars

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as cars
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars in traffic.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Eight times
Ten times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a crash with head injuries than riding without one.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have curved, or convex, mirrors. What do these mirrors do?

options.text: Are easy to use right away
Make cars look closer than they are
Show a narrow view of the road
Make cars look farther away than they are

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars look farther away than they are
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give a wider view of the road behind you. They make objects look farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances if you are not used to them.

questions.question: What type of sign can be rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular and white with black lettering. They show traffic rules that you must follow.

questions.question: When do you NOT need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When the road is slippery
When there is heavy traffic
When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
When it is raining

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy. You do not need extra distance when you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: If your front wheel starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Keep using the front brake and ride out the skid
Keep using the front brake and release the rear brake
Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake immediately and then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed
Avoid making sudden moves
Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shade, and bridges—these areas are more slippery.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids from braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front brake engaged
Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake
Release both brakes and coast to a stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks from braking, release the front brake immediately and apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other
Do both at the same time and brake harder
Do both at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving
Do not do either action

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. You need good grip to swerve safely. If you must brake and swerve, do one action first and then the other.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often alcohol is consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Your sex, physical condition, and food intake may also matter. How often you drink does not affect your current BAC.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Increase your speed.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil deposits that are slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. Also, slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without making inexperienced riders lead the group.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: Switching into a neutral gear.
When you will be slowing down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will be slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before you slow down suddenly. A driver following too closely may be focused on you and may not see hazards ahead that are making you slow down.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, why should you ride on the left side of your lane?

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
It gives you a better view of hazards in the next lane.
People don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
It places you in the rearview mirror of the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a better view of hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of your lane improves your view and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic when passing on the left.
